frog_0004.fact: The liver of a frog contains 3 lobes which help secrete its digestive juices called bile.

frog_0005.fact: Frogs can hold their breath for an average of 4 to 7 hours at a time.

frog_0006.fact: Frogs lay their eggs in the water much as toads do.

frog_0001.fact: Since the 1970s, over 200 frog species have been considered to be extinct.

frog_0002.fact: As of 2015, there are over 6000 different frog species that have been discovered.

frog_0003.fact: Frogs have 3 distinctive cavities in their bodies that host their organs.

frog_0007.fact: The Goliath Frog is said to be the largest species of frogs in the world.

frog_0008.fact: Frogs and toads are not considered to be the same animal but are considered to be similar.

frog_0009.fact: The smallest frog species in the world is known as the Paedophryne amanuensis .

frog_0010.fact: The largest organ in the body of a frog is its liver.

frog_0011.fact: Many frogs have special toe pads that allow them to stick onto surfaces without falling.

frog_0012.fact: In some eastern countries, frogs are typically consumed as street food or in prepared dishes.

frog_0013.fact: The skin of a frog can vary in color from green, brown, black, orange, blue, and many others.

frog_0014.fact: Frogs are classified as social animals that typically live in groups referred to as an army.

frog_0015.fact: Frogs have two slits at the bottom of their mouths that allow them to croak with their vocal cords.

frog_0016.fact: There are approximately 170 different types of poison dart frogs.

frog_0017.fact: The tongue of a frog is typically ⅓ of the length of its body.

frog_0018.fact: Around 466 frog species are classified to be critically endangered.

frog_0019.fact: One of the most common animals seen in the world are frogs. Despite their size, frogs are considered to be quite the opponent in the wild due to their excellent survival and camouflage skills. Frogs are also an important part of the food chain as they are both the predator and prey. Find out more about these cute and slimy creatures with our collection of frog facts.

frog_0020.fact: The Darwin’s frog is a small frog species that are typically classified by their elongated snout which gives their head a triangular appearance. When a female Darwin’s frog lays its eggs , the male will guard them for a period of 3 to 4 weeks by storing them in its vocal cords until the embryos begin to move.

frog_0021.fact: The tadpoles inside the male frog will feed off of their egg yolks and other secretions that are produced by the wall of the vocal sac until the stage of metamorphosis. Once this stage has been reached, the tadpoles will have turned into frogs by then and jump out of their father’s mouth and disperse.
